question: I'm heading off on a two-month trip to Australia over Christmas and the house will be completely empty. Do I need to let you know beforehand, and what do I have to do with the heating or water so I'm still covered if a pipe bursts?
expected: Yes. Tell your broker if the home will be unoccupied for over 60 days. For escape of water while unoccupied, keep the heating at a minimum of 10C from November to March, or turn off and drain the water system
author: written independently of the glossary

question: My dog just chewed through the bottom of a brand-new leather sofa and scratched up the wooden door frame. Am I covered for pet damage under my buildings or contents, and is there a limit?
expected: Yes, damage by chewing, scratching, tearing, vomiting or fouling by pets is covered but limited to £5,000 under contents and £5,000 under buildings
author: written independently of the glossary

question: Someone smashed the window of my car while it was parked at the supermarket and stole my backpack from the back seat. Can I claim for my stolen stuff on my Basic home contents policy?
expected: No. Theft from vehicle is not covered on Basic (Silver and Gold only)
author: written independently of the glossary

question: I'm planning to renovate my kitchen next month, just ripping out the old units and fitting new ones without knocking down any walls. Do I have to tell you before the builders start?
expected: Yes. Policy Expert must be told about any building work, conversions or renovations at least 30 days before it starts; only redecoration is exempt
author: written independently of the glossary

question: My son is moving into university halls in September with his laptop and musical instruments. Are his things covered under my home contents policy while he's away at uni, and what if someone steals them from his room?
expected: Student belongings in halls or term-time accommodation are covered up to the amount in the schedule; theft is only covered if there is evidence of forcible and violent entry
author: written independently of the glossary

question: Last night's storm blew down two panels of my garden fence and knocked over my shed. Will my buildings insurance cover the cost of replacing the fence and fixing the shed?
expected: Storm damage to gates, hedges and fences is excluded, so not the fence. The shed is part of the buildings and is not excluded from storm cover
author: written independently of the glossary
